title: The Executive Sheet records each change twice, as Input Action and Derived Action, each with its own Reasoning and Authority URL
content:
A.1.10.2.3.2.1.3.1 specifies how a module deployment enters the Executive Sheet. The "Input Action" "describes the high level logic of the Deployment, for example 'Add [Module Name] to Chainlog'" and its Reasoning URL points to the Atlas Edit Proposal forum post while its Authority URL points to Atlas documents. The "Derived Action" "is more specific for deployment address and other necessary information," and its Reasoning URL points to the Technical Scope Forum post while its Authority URL points to the Core Facilitator's approval.

Read as a schema, every on-chain change carries four independent links: *why in principle*, *who says it is permitted in principle*, *why these specific bytes*, and *who says these specific bytes are permitted*.

The reason to split rather than collapse them is that the two levels fail differently. An Input Action can be legitimate while its Derived Action is wrong — a correct decision pointed at the wrong address. Because the Derived Action must carry its own authority link (the Core Facilitator's explicit approval of *this* deployment), a concrete parameter cannot silently borrow the legitimacy of the abstract intent above it.

The distinct sources are also deliberate: abstract authority comes from the Atlas (a governed document), concrete authority comes from a named human's public approval. Verifying an Executive Vote therefore means checking a documentary chain, not reading intentions — and a break in the chain is locatable at a specific slot.
description: Provenance becomes a four-slot data structure: high-level intent and concrete parameters are justified and authorized separately, so a wrong address cannot inherit the intent's authorization.
